summary:
LunArk: Genesis is a free, open-source Moon-base management game for ages 7-12. Players run a small lunar outpost and learn that a crewed base needs more than rockets. It needs power, research, money and a crew that stays motivated.

What the player does

Build and manage 13 modules: a habitat, power generators, revenue buildings, activity buildings and science buildings.
Balance five indicators: Energy, Science, Boredom, Revenue and Event.
Survive the lunar day-and-night cycle, when solar power stops and heating drains the battery.
Respond to six hazards: solar flares, micrometeorites, lunar dust, crew conflict, equipment failure and care packages. Each gives a warning, and players can shield buildings, clean dust and repair equipment.
Win by completing Planet Stats research and surviving three full cycles.

Why it matters
It turns real lunar-surface challenges into decisions a child can make. Tutorial text uses plain language and explains each science term the first time it appears. Win and lose screens explain what happened and give a hint, so failure teaches something.

Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. All art is drawn by hand in Aseprite by the team.
AI disclosure: code was written by AI coding agents (Google Antigravity, using Gemini and Claude models) from prompts planned with Claude. The team directed and reviewed the work.

Summary
LunArk: Genesis is a free, open-source Moon-base management game for ages 7-12. Players run a small lunar outpost and learn that a crewed base needs more than rockets. It needs power, research, money and a crew that stays motivated.

What the player does

  • Build and manage 13 modules: a habitat, power generators, revenue buildings, activity buildings and science buildings.
  • Balance five indicators: Energy, Science, Boredom, Revenue and Event.
  • Survive the lunar day-and-night cycle, when solar power stops and heating drains the battery.
  • Respond to six hazards: solar flares, micrometeorites, lunar dust, crew conflict, equipment failure and care packages. Each gives a warning, and players can shield buildings, clean dust and repair equipment.
  • Win by completing Planet Stats research and surviving three full cycles.

Why it matters
It turns real lunar-surface challenges into decisions a child can make. Tutorial text uses plain language and explains each science term the first time it appears. Win and lose screens explain what happened and give a hint, so failure teaches something.

How it was made

  • Python and pygame-ce, with a hand-drawn pixel-art style. Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
  • All art is drawn by hand in Aseprite by the team.
  • AI disclosure: code was written by AI coding agents (Google Antigravity, using Gemini and Claude models) from prompts planned with Claude. The team directed and reviewed the work.
  • Provenance: the display engine, settings menu, title screen and logo art were first made in October, before the event. The README lists everything done during Nov 14-15.
  • Released under GPL-3.0.
